items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: This group was called the "Chaussettes Noires" (black socks) and featuring a young singer named Eddie Mitchell.

ctx.x: The day after our arrival, I had rehearsal with the band and it was terrible. We tried for two hours to rehearse "Caravan" and another number but it was must impossible. Most of those kids couldn't read, and they had no experience at all. It would have taken weeks to try to teach them to play correctly a dozen numbers. I went to see Badel and told him to look for another band. He wanted to put the blame on me because I had accepted to play with them in Paris. I wanted to put the blame on him because we had told…

Every night before my first passage, a group of young rock and rollers were playing for a half hour. It was the beginning in France of the rock and roll era. This group was called the "Chaussettes Noires" (black socks) and featuring a young singer named Eddie Mitchell.

So every night we were going through the same routine. A crowd of about 100 very young teenagers was waiting outside of the "Vieux Colombier". At 9.30 the waiters were letting them in without paying entrance fee. I was even told that at the beginning, they were paid a small fee. They would stand against the walls and they started to shout hysterically: we want "the Chaussette Noires". The group began to play encouraged by frantic shouts from their supporters.
